[Email](mailto:loris.lombardi.jp@gmail.com) · [ORCID](https://orcid.org/0009-0002-4915-1750) · [GitHub](https://github.com/lolonifuji) · [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/lorislombardi)

I am a PhD candidate in International and Advanced Japanese Studies at the
University of Tsukuba. My research applies computational text analysis to
Japanese online discourse, with a focus on toxicity, hate speech, and
political communication.

My dissertation is a computational study of hostility in Japanese anonymous
news commentary, based on a complete corpus of 5channel's Newsplus board
(2017–2026). It combines large-scale text analysis with human-in-the-loop
annotation to measure toxicity and hate speech in Japanese. Alongside the
dissertation, I work on public discourse around AI and emerging technologies
in Japan, and on quantitative analysis of National Diet records.

Research interests: computational political communication; Japanese online
discourse; online hostility, toxicity and hate speech; framing and agenda
setting; AI discourse in Japan; text-as-data methods for Japanese.
